A1.evidence: The code is retrievable via HTTPS from the article landing page per Row 6's entitlement ('HTTPS delivery via the article landing page'). The data-completeness A1 override in the instrument is explicitly scoped to data ('A1 = 0 for data FAIR'); it does not apply to code_fair, which is scored on its own base A1 definition here.

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS delivery (Row 6 entitlement) is an open, free, universally implementable protocol.

A1_2.evidence: Same reasoning as the data Supplement: neither the paper nor the evidence pack nor Row 6's entitlement addresses whether authentication is required to retrieve the code file specifically. Genuinely silent rather than affirmatively open; defaults to 0 under the unscoreable-boundary rule.

F1.evidence: The authors' own code (OxCal model script + R code calling ArchaeoPhases, per Author's Contributions: 'AP ... improved the R code for tempo and occurrence plots') is 'included in the Supplement' (p. 11), distributed under the article DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765 per F1's declared departure clause for supplement-distributed artefacts.

F2.evidence: Row 6, explicit: 'F2 = F3 = F4 = 0 ... for supplement-only deposits'; the evidence pack confirms the supplement is declared under the bare article-DOI link with no independent deposit/metadata record.

F3.evidence: Row 6, explicit: no independent metadata record exists to include an identifier reference.

F4.evidence: Row 6, explicit: no registry indexing for supplement-only deposits; the code is not separately registered on CRAN, Software Heritage, Zenodo, or similar. (The evidence pack's CRAN lookup is for the third-party ArchaeoPhases dependency, not the authors' own scripts, and is itself unresolved — 'endpoint-flagged' per erratum-log Entry 3 item 8.)

I1.evidence: The OxCal model script and the R/ArchaeoPhases plotting code are both structured, plain-text, machine-parseable formal scripting languages, not PDF or unstructured prose.

I2.evidence: No evidence of FAIR-compliant controlled-vocabulary or ontology use within the code itself.

I3.evidence: The paper gives a full, DOI-bearing citation to the code's key dependency: 'Philippe, A., & Vibet, M.-A. (2020). Analysis of archaeological phases using the CRAN package ArchaeoPhases. Journal of Statistical Software, 93. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v093.c01' (references, p. 28), and the Conclusion explicitly attributes functionality to it: 'functions provided by ArchaeoPhases software (Philippe & Vibet, 2020)' (p. 23). Only one principal code artefact exists (the authors' own scripts), so no conjunctive-scoring ambiguity arises here.

R1.evidence: The paper documents the code's function and structure in detail: the OxCal model's two-section composition (likelihoods/constraints; per-bead-type occurrences, p. 11), and explicit statements that 'ArchaeoPhases code to reproduce the figure is included in the Supplement' for both Figure 3 and Figure 4 captions (p. 13, p. 15).

R1_1.evidence: Same reasoning as data R1.1: no code-specific licence is stated; default-to-same-as-article applies (Row 6, rule (a)); the Elsevier VoR's Crossref-recorded licences are TDM-only policy links, not a reuse licence, and the White Rose CC-BY-NC-ND licence is explicitly scoped to the article-text repository copy, not the Elsevier-hosted Supplement.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed software/methodological provenance is documented: OxCal v4.4.2, IntCal20 calibration curve, three enumerated prior-constraint removals with rationale, a 5-independent-run stability check, and full citation of the ArchaeoPhases dependency with version-identifying DOI.

R1_3.evidence: No evidence of CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review (CRAN/JOSS/rOpenSci) for the authors' own scripts — they are undifferentiated supplementary files, not a packaged/reviewed software release. The instrument explicitly excludes OxCal as a qualifying standard ('Methodological standards (IntCal20, OxCal, established methods) do NOT qualify'). The ArchaeoPhases dependency's own CRAN/JOSS standing (Philippe & Vibet 2020, Journal of Statistical Software) is a third-party artefact and, per the aggregation rule, 'third-party dependencies are never substitutes for [the paper's own principal code]... enter scoring only through citation quality (I3) and the evidence pack' — it does not transfer to satisfy R1.3 for the authors' own scripts.

barriers: Closed monograph: Nielsen (2013) 'Typology' chapter (bead identification/classification scheme) in Hines & Bayliss (2013), Society for Medieval Archaeology — no PID, no online-access evidence in paper or evidence pack; explicitly named by the paper (p. 10) as one of the four reasons the bead data were selected for phyletic seriation, i.e. necessary to interpret which finds belong to which bead type.

Colleague/gatekeeping access: the RAF Lakenheath source underlying Hines (2021) (contributing 20 of 72 graves, ~28% of the seriation sample) was obtained via personal request rather than standard retrieval — Acknowledgments (p. 24): 'John Hines for informative correspondence and supplying a copy of the Lakenheath report.' No dataset PID or open-access link is given for this source anywhere in the paper.

A1.evidence: Instrument rule: 'If data_completeness coverage is minimal or partial, A1 = 0... Exception: ethical restrictions.' data_completeness.coverage_category = 'partial' (60%), driven by the closed-monograph (Nielsen 2013 typology) and gatekept-access (Hines 2021/Lakenheath report obtained by personal correspondence, p. 24) barriers — neither is a documented ethical/legal restriction, so the exception does not apply. The override therefore sets A1=0 for data, notwithstanding that the two digital deposits actually held (ADS DOI resolution; Supplement HTTPS via Row 6) would individually support standard-protocol retrievability.

A1_1.evidence: For the accessible portion of the data (per fair-principles-guide: A1.1 is evaluated 'for the accessible portion'): the ADS archive resolves via DOI/HTTPS (evidence pack, datacite endpoint, http_status 200), and the Supplement is delivered via HTTPS from the article landing page per Row 6's entitlement. Both use an open, free, universally implementable protocol.

A1_2.evidence: ADS individually appears open with no authentication barrier (licence field reads 'ADS Terms and Conditions apply to reuse', a reuse-conduct condition rather than an access/login gate; DataCite resolution succeeded via the public API). However, for the Supplement, neither the paper text nor the evidence pack nor Row 6's entitlement ('HTTPS delivery via the article landing page' only) speaks to whether authentication/subscription is required to retrieve the Elsevier-hosted supplementary file — this is genuinely silent, not affirmatively 'fully open' or affirmatively 'gated'. Per the unscoreable-boundary rule this defaults to 0 for the Supplement, and conjunctive scoring across both principal artefacts fails.

A2.evidence: Row 1 (DataCite, applicable to the ADS DOI): 'NOT guaranteed: public metadata accessibility after withdrawal.' Row 4's ADS-specific entry adds no separate persistence entitlement. For the Supplement, Row 6 is explicit: 'A2 = 0 for supplement-only deposits.' Both principal artefacts fail/are unestablished; conjunctive A2 = 0.

F1.evidence: Two principal data artefacts, conjunctively assessed. (1) Hines (2013) ADS archive has its own DOI 10.5284/1018290, confirmed resolved via DataCite ('state': 'findable', http_status 200) in the evidence pack. (2) The paper's own revised OxCal model/occurrence data is 'included in the Supplement' (p. 11) of the article, distributed under the article DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765 — satisfying F1's declared departure clause for supplement-under-article-DOI. Both hold.

F2.evidence: ADS individually would score 1 (DataCite record with structured fields plus Row 4's ingest-enforced core template), but the Supplement fails: evidence pack shows the 'supplement' artefact is declared under the same bare article-DOI link as the 'article', with no independent metadata record. Instrument Row 6 is explicit: 'NO independent metadata record, licence field, registry indexing, or resource-level identifier — hence F2 = F3 = F4 = 0 ... for supplement-only deposits.' Conjunctive scoring requires both principal artefacts to hold; it fails.

F3.evidence: Same conjunctive failure as F2: ADS metadata does include the identifier (evidence pack field identifier_in_metadata: true), but the Supplement has no independent metadata record to include one, per Row 6's explicit F3=0 rule for supplement-only deposits.

F4.evidence: ADS is DataCite-indexed and independently searchable, but the Supplement is not registered/indexed anywhere independent of the article landing page (Row 6: F4=0 for supplement-only deposits). Conjunctive requirement fails.

I1.evidence: Both principal artefacts use a formal, structured representation: the ADS deposit is described as 'a relational database deposited with the Archaeological Data Service that catalogs the graves and the finds' (p. 10); the paper's own revised chronological model is 'implemented in OxCal' (p. 11), a structured, machine-parseable domain scripting syntax, not PDF/prose. Both hold.

I2.evidence: No evidence in the paper or evidence pack that either artefact uses a published, PID-bearing controlled vocabulary or ontology (e.g. Getty AAT, PeriodO, CIDOC-CRM) for the bead-type classification or grave records; the BE1-* type codes derive from an internal typology (Nielsen 2013), not a FAIR-compliant external vocabulary.

I3.evidence: The paper explicitly states a typed derivation relationship with a resolvable PID: 'Chronological relations among the female graves are based on a chronological prior from the OxCal model deposited in the project archive (Hines, 2013)' (p. 10), and the reference list gives the full DOI (https://doi.org/10.5284/1018290). This is a qualified ('based on'/derived-from) reference from the paper's own data output to a related PID-bearing resource. Applied to the data research surface as a whole (a judgement call on how a relational sub-principle interacts with conjunctive per-artefact scoring, since the ADS record's own metadata fields as shown in the evidence pack do not themselves list relatedIdentifiers).

R1.evidence: ADS: Row 4 entitlement, 'mandatory validated core template plus category-specific technical metadata, enforced at ingest.' Supplement: the paper gives an unusually detailed account of its structure and content — 'It comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (p. 11) — functioning as extended documentation of the deposited materials. Both hold.

R1_1.evidence: ADS individually has a stated licence field ('ADS Terms and Conditions apply to reuse'). For the Supplement, instrument R1.1 rule (a): 'absent a separate supplement licence, default to same-as-paper.' No supplement-specific licence is stated anywhere in the paper. The relevant 'paper' for a publisher-hosted supplement served from the article landing page is the Elsevier VoR, whose Crossref-recorded licences are exclusively TDM-only policy links (https://doi.org/10.15223/policy-004 etc., elsevier.com/legal/tdmrep-license, elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0/) — text-and-data-mining carve-outs, not a general reuse/data-usage licence. (The CC-BY-NC-ND licence on p. 1 explicitly scopes to 'this repository copy' of the article text at White Rose Research Online, a separate green-OA channel that does not host or licence the Supplement.) No clear, accessible data-usage licence is therefore established for the Supplement; conjunctive R1.1 fails.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance is documented for the Supplement: OxCal version 4.4.2, the IntCal20 calibration curve (Reimer et al. 2020), three specific prior constraints removed with stated rationale (i-iii, p. 10-11), and a validation step ('five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability', p. 11). ADS: Row 4 ingest-enforced technical metadata template plausibly carries creator/method/date fields. Both hold.

R1_3.evidence: ADS scores 1-by-construction per Row 4: 'ADS ... an ingest-enforced domain metadata standard; R1.3 = 1 by construction.' The Supplement fails: the instrument's own R1.3 section explicitly excludes the relevant standard — 'Methodological standards (IntCal20, OxCal, established methods) do NOT qualify' — and OxCal is named verbatim as a non-qualifying example. Conjunctive scoring requires both; it fails.
